title: Connect an existing AI subscription
summary: Review official CLI installation and learn the exact login and connection flow for Claude, Codex, or Grok.
prerequisites: Install Instrilo v0.2.3 or newer from a release and prepare the tutorial workspace as shown below.
Use Bash on macOS/Linux or WSL on Windows. Run all commands inside your prepared tutorial workspace in the same terminal.
The bundled verify.mjs helper only reads the tutorial outputs and checks the expected facts. All agent actions still use the visible Instrilo commands.
outcome: Reviewed installation plans and a project ready for your chosen provider.

verification.scope: The plans, help commands, and offline project creation run automatically. Provider-owned installation and login are separate manual steps.
limitations: No real account is signed in by this walkthrough test.
A subscription does not grant interchangeable API credentials or permission to run its CLI in a hosted container.
Grok has no verified persistent auth-status command; successful login alone is not proof a model call will succeed.

steps.title: Read the workflow and create a local project
steps.body: The installed CLI stays under your user account. Instrilo uses official provider login; do not paste browser session tokens into your manifest.
steps.code:
set -eu
INSTRILO_PROJECT=.studio/tutorials/subscription-setup
instrilo init subscription-setup --directory .studio/tutorials
instrilo explain subscriptions
instrilo setup --help
instrilo connect --help
steps.expected: The project is created in offline demo mode. Help explains installation consent, device login, roles, and connection choices.

steps.title: Review all three install plans
steps.body: These commands only show the exact official npm package, destination, and registry. They do not download packages, start login, or call a model.
steps.code:
instrilo auth install codex --plan > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/codex-plan.json"
instrilo auth install claude --plan > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/claude-plan.json"
instrilo auth install grok --plan > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/grok-plan.json"
node examples/quickstarts/delivery/verify.mjs install-plans "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: All three plans name their expected official package. Open the saved JSON files to inspect the destination and command.

steps.title: Choose one provider and sign in
steps.body: Optional account step: choose ONE line below. The terminal asks before installation and starts that provider’s own login if needed. You need an eligible account, network access, and permission to install user-local npm packages. The walkthrough does not verify your account or provider allowance.
steps.manualCode:
instrilo setup codex
# Or: instrilo setup claude
# Or: instrilo setup grok
steps.expected: The official tool completes sign-in, or prints an actionable account, dependency, or terminal requirement. Codex/Grok can use --device if their browser login is inconvenient; Claude has no verified device option.

steps.title: Connect the role you want and make an explicit live check
steps.body: Optional account step: this example uses Codex. Substitute claude or grok consistently if you chose it. Connecting the builder leaves runtime/judge on demo until you select them too. Verification makes one bounded model request and can consume account allowance or API billing depending on provider credentials.
steps.manualCode:
instrilo connect codex .studio/tutorials/subscription-setup --role builder
instrilo auth status codex
instrilo auth verify codex
# Optional local native runtime or judge:
# instrilo connect codex .studio/tutorials/subscription-setup --role runtime
# instrilo connect claude .studio/tutorials/subscription-setup --role judge
steps.expected: connect saves the selected named connection. auth verify reports verified:true only when that live request returns the exact verification marker. Status alone does not verify quota or future billing.

next.label: Give the judge its own connection

troubleshooting: Use a fresh tutorial project name if init says the directory already exists. The commands create files and reports that deliberately refuse overwriting existing results.
Read the printed error and instrilo help --all before retrying. A failed assertion means the observed result differs from this guide.
If a CLI is missing, setup offers its reviewed installation. If the detected CLI is old, read the plan and update the provider tool before retrying.
To cancel login, press Ctrl+C. Do not copy login codes or session links into a public issue.
cleanup: The tutorial creates only its named project under .studio/tutorials. Keep reports if useful; remove that project directory when you no longer need it.
This guide’s tested steps install nothing. Official provider credentials and previously installed tools remain yours; deleting the tutorial project does not sign you out.
